Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines - capacity uplift & term change

Hi Sergio —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Orbit is excited to move forward with the capacity uplift into Q3, and procurement asked me to send the attached redlines so our legal and finance teams can align. High level: we need a 12-month term (instead of 24), an immediate 2x capacity increase for the first 3 months, and a clause clarifying data residency for logs (EU only for EU-tenanted workloads).

Attached: Orbit_MSA_redlines_v2.pdf (redlines in PDF) and a draft order form with proposed quantities.

Primary asks:
- Can Redwood accept a 12-month initial term with an automatic renewal unless terminated?
- Can you confirm the capacity lead time for dedicated pools and whether burst capacity can be capped per month?
- We flagged indemnity language around telemetry—can legal review the struck text and propose an alternative?

Marcus will be looping in procurement for payment timing. Would you and your legal lead take the redlines and propose a clean mark?

Appreciate it,
Elena

Elena —

Thanks for sending this over and for the call. I’ve shared the PDF with our contracts team and looped in Kimberly (legal) and Vanessa (customer success / billing) to handle the term and capacity questions. Quick responses while they review:

- 12-month initial term: we can usually do 12 months; there are a few pricing and SLA considerations for shorter initial terms which Kimberly will outline.
- Dedicated capacity lead time: typical provisioning is 7-10 business days for a standard pool; for a 2x surge we can offer burst capacity but we’ll want a monthly cap to avoid runaway costs — Vanessa will propose a cap and the associated price.
- Data residency: we support EU-resident logging for EU tenants and can add a clause to the order form; Kimberly, can legal propose language that satisfies Orbit’s asks while keeping our telemetry exception for troubleshooting?

I’ll turn this to you by EOD tomorrow with suggested language and a redlined order form.

Best,

Hi all —

I reviewed Orbit_MSA_redlines_v2.pdf and put together a short set of proposed edits (see summary below). I will attach a cleaned redline PDF via DocuSign link once you confirm the principal points.

Summary of proposed changes (high level):
1) Term & Renewal — Accept 12-month initial term. Propose explicit auto-renewal for successive 12-month periods unless either party gives 60 days’ notice. For revenue recognition and uplift pricing, add a schedule that locks pricing for the initial term.

2) Capacity & Burst — Agree to a 2x uplift for the first 3 months as a one-time committed increase on the order form. For burst beyond committed capacity, propose a capped burst pool charged at a premium per token-hour; recommend Orbit pick a monthly burst cap in the order form to protect both sides.

3) Data Residency & Telemetry — We can accept requirement that persistent logs for EU tenants are stored in EU regions. We cannot fully remove telemetry exceptions needed for incident triage; propose language that limits telemetry to ephemeral debugging traces and requires prior notice for production log dumps.

4) Indemnity & Liability — Orbit requested softer language. We can narrow the indemnity carve-out to third-party IP claims and will not change the core limitation of liability; propose a mutual carve-in for negligence up to a negotiated cap.

Next steps: Vanessa, can you draft the revised order form numbers (committed capacity, burst cap, and pricing delta)? Elena/Marcus, once we have numbers and the cleaned redline I’ll prepare a mark for signature.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Kim / Sergio —

Thanks for the quick review — the summary looks good. Procurement is comfortable with a 60-day renewal notice and a 12-month initial term. For the burst cap, Orbit prefers a monthly burst cap of 10% above committed Q3 capacity at a premium rate rather than an open cap. Please reflect that in the order form pricing.

On payment terms: Orbit is requesting net 60 for the first invoice due to internal PO cycles; happy to discuss a smaller invoice on signature and the remainder spread over the term.

Elena, can you confirm if Net-60 will work operationally?

Thanks,
Marcus
